title: Photosynthesis & limiting factors
examples: What is the word equation for photosynthesis?
How does changing the light level affect plant growth?
If I keep the temperature constant, what limits the rate of photosynthesis?

explain.say: Photosynthesis is the process plants use to make food. It uses sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.
The word equation shows the reactants and the products clearly. Plants need light, water, and carbon dioxide to start.
Light intensity is one key factor affecting the rate. As light increases, the rate increases too.
Carbon dioxide concentration is another factor that matters greatly. More carbon dioxide means a faster rate.
Temperature affects the rate because enzymes need the right warmth to work best. Too cold or too hot slows things down.
In real life, if you grow plants indoors, you must consider all these factors. You need enough light, water, and air.

faq.q: What is the limiting factor in photosynthesis?
faq.a: The limiting factor is the one resource that is in the smallest amount. It controls how fast the whole process can go.
asks: What limits the rate of photosynthesis?
Which factor is the bottleneck for plant energy production?

faq.q: Does the rate always increase when I add more light?
faq.a: No, the rate will increase up to a certain point. After that, another factor, like CO₂, might become the limit.
asks: When does light stop being the limit?
Can adding light always help plants grow faster?

faq.q: Why is the optimum temperature important?
faq.a: Enzymes, which speed up reactions, work best within a specific temperature range. Too far outside this range, they stop working well.
asks: What happens to enzymes in extreme heat?
Is there a perfect temperature for plants?

faq.q: If I increase CO₂ but keep light low, what happens?
faq.a: The rate will not increase much because the light is not providing enough energy. Light remains the limiting factor in this case.
asks: Can CO₂ compensate for low light?
If light is low, does CO₂ matter?

faq.q: What is the role of water in the equation?
faq.a: Water is split during the process, releasing oxygen. It is a necessary reactant for the chemical reaction to occur.
asks: Is water just something the plant drinks?
Does water go into the equation?

facts: The word equation shows the inputs and outputs of photosynthesis.
Light intensity, CO₂ concentration, and temperature can limit the rate.
The rate of photosynthesis increases until a factor becomes limiting.
Enzymes function optimally within a specific temperature range.

quiz.say: If light is very low, increasing the CO₂ will cause:
quiz.why: Light energy is needed to power the reaction, so adding more CO₂ has no effect.

wrong.0: This is too simple; the rate is limited by the weakest link, not just staying the same.
wrong.1: There is no reason for the rate to decrease when the other factors are still low.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the process needs light energy first, like turning on a switch.

quiz.say: Which factor usually limits the rate at very high temperatures?
quiz.why: High temperatures can damage the enzymes needed for the chemical reactions to happen.

wrong.0: Water is usually available unless the plant is severely dehydrated.
wrong.2: Temperature affects the enzymes directly, not just the light source.
wrong.3: While CO₂ is important, the physical structure of the enzymes breaks down first.

quiz.say: If the graph shows the rate peaking and then falling, this pattern is most likely due to changes in:
quiz.why: The characteristic bell shape of the rate curve is typical when temperature affects enzyme function.

wrong.0: Water limitation usually causes a steady, gradual drop, not a sharp peak and fall.
wrong.2: Light usually causes a curve that flattens out, not one that falls sharply.
wrong.3: Increasing CO₂ usually leads to a plateau, not a sharp decline.
